label: .github/workflows/sk-git-script-tests.yml has exactly one suite step (worktree-naming.test.sh at line 51) while .skilled/skills/sk-git/scripts/tests/ holds five suites (commit-id-naming, migrate-legacy-branch-names, stamp-branch, validate-message-git-timeout.test.mjs, worktree-naming), so the commit-id rules (v4.0.0.3/v4.0.0.10) and the wedged-git timeout (v4.0.0.16) have regression tests CI never runs; sk-git/scripts/hooks/git-preflight-advisory.test.mjs is doubly unwired because it sits outside tests/; sk-code-script-tests.yml enumerates five distinct commands by contrast, so this is one unwidened workflow, not a convention.

/doctor:overlay status with --json and engine exit 2 is governed by two mutually exclusive presentation lines: line 101 says print the engine JSON and nothing around it, line 379's error template says render STATUS=FAIL ERROR="[code]", while doctor-overlay-status.yaml:58 requires the exit be mapped to a route status; a scripted consumer sees a STATUS token on exit 0/1 and none on exit 2, and the route contract never says which line wins.

The overlay engine throws 'no overlay manifest at ...' from two sites (line 433 with the .skilled-overlays.json suffix, line 437 without it), but the presentation contract's remedy row assumes the suffixed variant, so a consumer on the bare throw gets a message with no hint that .skilled-overlays.json is the setting file.

status is the default_target of /doctor:overlay and declared read-only, but the Skilled source checkout has neither skilled-overlays/ nor .skilled-overlays.json, so a bare /doctor:overlay in the tree that ships the command always ends STATUS=ERROR with a remedy ('add .skilled-overlays.json at the tree root') that is wrong for a source repo; the contract's <overlay folder> placeholder also names two different folders on the same page.

ci-toggle.cjs states unconditionally that a change to the state the variable already has is refused as a no-op, but with gh unavailable the plan reports current=unknown and noChange=false and still emits the gh variable set command, so the plan cannot distinguish 'variable is on' from 'not checked'; the ruleset check degrades honestly with a reason field while the no-op refusal does not.

sk-git/scripts/tests/README.md still says tests/ holds the harness for worktree-naming.sh alone, which is accurate for what CI runs and wrong for the directory's five files; the README was not widened when the later suites landed.
